correct_completion: he always drinks tea in the morning.
full_sentence: Because Tom never drinks coffee, he always drinks tea in the morning.
acceptable_variants: he usually orders green tea at cafes.

options.text: he sometimes drinks coffee at night.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts 'never' in the stem, so it cannot be a logical result of it.

options.text: he always drinks tea in the morning.
he is always hungry at lunchtime.
options.why_wrong: This is unrelated to drinks, so it does not complete the cause-effect link set up by 'because'.

options.text: he has drunk coffee since he was a child.
options.why_wrong: This directly contradicts 'never' in the stem.

grammar_focus: Cause-effect clauses with 'because' and adverbs of frequency
explanation: After 'because', the main clause must show a logical result of the first part. Since Tom never drinks coffee, the result should be a habit that replaces it. The frequency adverb goes before the main verb in English. Portuguese speakers may place the adverb after the verb, which sounds unnatural in English.
translation: Como Tom nunca bebe café, ele sempre toma chá de manhã.
